correctness.rationale: Re-derived Kirchhoff index n tr((L+J/n)^-1)-n; graph simple ensures any nonzero conductance perturbation gives H≠0, and second derivative 2n tr(Q^-1 H Q^-1 H Q^-1)>0. Reflection symmetry excludes paired ordinary-edge zeros, and a hypothetical opposite ordinary zero (even n) has path-end voltage gain/budget multiplier at least 2n/(n-1)>1, contradicting unit-price KKT. The closing-zero path is optimized by Cauchy–Schwarz with w_k=B sqrt(k(n-k))/S_n. The missing closing edge derivative is multiplier times n Σ(T_j-mean T)^2, giving iff via strict convexity and complementary slackness, including equality. Symmetric endpoint-singular Riemann sums converge to 2 arcsin√x, and the centered squared integral is pi^2/4-2. Independent numerical values give r_c(3)=3 and r_c(4)=11/3+4/sqrt3; at n=600 normalized value approaches the stated limit. Finite checks do not prove all n.
